RE: Formal Internal Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination

Member: Morgan Brooks (ID: W188108937)
Requested Service: Total knee replacement, CPT 27447
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-12
Appeal Deadline: 2027-02-08

Dear Appeals Review Team,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for total knee replacement (CPT 27447), as set forth in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-12 (Reference # POC-5585B8DEE7-94152). The stated reason for denial was that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." I am submitting this appeal, together with my surgeon's records, to show that the documentation in my file does in fact establish medical necessity.

Oscar has identified its own governing coverage document for this procedure as the clinical guideline titled "Total Knee Arthroplasty (Replacement)," policy number CG069. I have not been provided the exact version number or effective date of CG069 that was applied to my specific denial, so I cannot confirm with certainty that the language quoted below is the exact version Oscar used. The quotations below are taken from a version of CG069 publicly available from Oscar. I am requesting, as part of this appeal, that Oscar confirm in writing which exact version and effective date of CG069 was applied to my prior authorization request, and identify specifically which criterion or criteria within it were found "incomplete."

Below, I address the general medical-necessity criteria set out in that document, and how the enclosed records address each element.

1. Advanced joint disease – imaging criterion
CG069 states that total knee arthroplasty is medically necessary where there are "Radiologic or arthroscopic findings of advanced knee joint destruction documented by the treating surgeon and/or radiologist for ONE of the following: i. Kellgren Lawrence Grade IV radiographic findings (Table 1)."

My weight-bearing knee radiographs, obtained 2026-07-01, document bone-on-bone apposition in the medial and patellofemoral compartments with lateral joint-space narrowing and a Kellgren-Lawrence Grade IV classification. This finding is enclosed in the imaging report and directly satisfies this criterion.

2. Severe, persistent pain interfering with function
CG069 requires "Severe pain persisting in the affected knee that interferes with functional activity or age-appropriate activities for at least 3 months (e.g., ambulation, prolonged standing, ability to sleep)."

My symptom duration is 9 months of progressive knee pain, unrelieved by rest. I am unable to climb stairs without assistance and wake 3–4 times nightly due to pain. My examination findings — varus alignment, crepitus, effusion, and range of motion limited to 5–100 degrees — are documented in the clinical exam notes enclosed. This satisfies the pain/functional-interference criterion.

3. Failure of a 3-month trial of conservative treatment
CG069 requires that "There has been a failure to decrease pain or improve function after at least a 3-month trial of conservative treatment (non-surgical) which has included ALL of the following":

a. "Active and ongoing participation in physical therapy (documented) or a well-documented home exercise program under the supervision of a physical therapist or physician (e.g., lower extremity flexibility and strengthening program, activity modification, and/or weight loss program), unless poorly tolerated or contraindicated."

I completed 10 weeks (2026-05-07 through 2026-07-16) of supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, totaling 18 visits, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note enclosed with this appeal.

b. "Oral/topical medications (e.g., analgesics, NSAIDs, serotonin/norepinephrine reuptake Inhibitor (duloxetine)), unless poorly tolerated or contraindicated."

I used NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief, as documented in my medication history.

c. The version of CG069 I was able to locate also references injection timing relative to the surgery date. I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-08, which provided only 3 weeks of partial relief. I am not able to state, without Oscar's confirmation of the exact policy version applied, whether this injection satisfies or conflicts with the specific injection-timing language in the version Oscar used. I ask that Oscar clarify this point directly, and I note that my surgeon can adjust the scheduled surgery date if needed to comply with any required interval between injection and surgery.

Together, these records show that I underwent and failed an adequate trial of conservative, non-surgical treatment — physical therapy, oral medication, and injection — over a period well in excess of 3 months, without adequate relief of pain or improvement in function.

4. Device/prosthesis FDA approval
CG069 states that "If there is a separate request for the device, implant or prosthesis that will be inserted during surgery, it must be FDA approved (unless the member is enrolled in an approved clinical trial as defined by the plan benefit)." My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, can provide manufacturer/device documentation confirming FDA approval of the planned implant if this was the specific element found "incomplete." [Device/implant documentation to be supplied by surgeon's office upon request.]

5. Absence of contraindications
The records in my file confirm no active knee or systemic infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and non-smoker status. I am not aware of any condition that would place me within the contraindication or "not medically necessary" categories described in CG069 (e.g., active infection, unmanaged joint instability, unmanaged anemia, or progressive neurologic disease affecting the lower extremity).

Requested Action
Because the enclosed clinical documentation directly addresses each of the general medical-necessity elements identified in CG069, I respectfully request that Oscar reverse the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 27447. In the alternative, if Oscar maintains that a specific criterion remains undocumented, I request a written, itemized explanation identifying exactly which criterion in the applicable version of CG069 was not met, so that my surgeon and I may supply the specific missing information within the applicable appeal timeframe.

Enclosures
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-07 to 2026-07-16, 18 visits)
- Medication history (NSAID trial, 4 months)
- Corticosteroid injection record (2026-06-08)
- Weight-bearing knee radiograph report (2026-07-01, Kellgren-Lawrence Grade IV)
- Clinical examination notes (range of motion, effusion, varus alignment)
- Letter of medical necessity from Okafor, MD, orthopedic surgery
- [Device/implant FDA-approval documentation, if applicable]

I am submitting this appeal within the 180-day window stated in the denial notice (by 2027-02-08). Please confirm receipt of this appeal and advise of any additional steps required.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Morgan Brooks
